import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Filter to significant features based on t-test
    sig_features = []
    for i, t_stat in enumerate(feats.types):
        if abs(t_stat) > 1.96:  # approximate significance threshold
            sig_features.append(i)
    
    # Remove near-duplicates
    keep = set()
    for i in sig_features:
        fid1 = feats.ids[i]
        dup = False
        for j in sig_features:
            if j <= i:
                continue
            fid2 = feats.ids[j]
            corr = abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:,i], feats.x[:,j])[0,1])
            if corr > 0.6:
                dup = True
                break
        if not dup:
            keep.add(i)
    
    # Select top features by effect size
    top_features = sorted(keep, key=lambda i: abs(feats.types[i]), reverse=True)[:MAX_DRIVERS]
    
    # If no strong signals, return empty design
    if len(top_features) == 0:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Fit logistic regression to get loadings
    X = feats.x[:, top_features]
    model = LogisticRegression(fit_intercept=False, max_iter=1000)
    model.fit(X, feats.y)
    
    # Get weights and sort by absolute value
    weights = model.coef_[0]
    ranked = sorted(zip(top_features, weights), key=lambda x: abs(x[1]), reverse=True)
    
    # Return top features as drivers and loadings
    drivers = tuple(feats.ids[i] for i, _ in ranked[:MAX_DRIVERS])
    columns = tuple(feats.ids[i] for i in top_features)
    loadings = {feats.ids[i]: w for i, w in ranked}
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=(), loadings=loadings)
